s: A company has 80 AWS accounts. Each account belongs to one of five business units, except a shared platform account where resources carry a BusinessUnit tag. The shared platform account also runs networking and security tooling that costs $40,000 per month and is used by all business units. Finance wants to filter costs by business unit in AWS Cost Explorer and AWS Budgets, and wants a monthly chargeback report that allocates the shared tooling costs in proportion to each business unit's own spend. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
o: Create a Cost Category for business units with rules based on linked accounts and the BusinessUnit tag. Add a split charge rule that allocates the shared tooling costs proportionally across the business-unit values.
Use AWS Billing Conductor to create a billing group for each business unit and a custom line item that divides the shared tooling costs.
Export CUR 2.0 data to Amazon S3, and build Amazon Athena queries and an Amazon QuickSight dashboard that allocate the shared costs each month.
Move each business unit's accounts into a separate OU, and filter AWS Cost Explorer by linked account for each OU.

w.y: AWS Cost Categories map costs by linked account and tag into business-unit values that appear natively in Cost Explorer and Budgets. Split charge rules allocate the shared tooling costs proportionally across those values, and the allocated results appear on the Cost Categories details page (downloadable as CSV), with no custom pipelines and the LEAST operational overhead.

o.A: Correct: native account/tag mapping usable in Cost Explorer and Budgets, plus proportional split charges reported in Cost Categories.
o.B: Billing groups are account-based, so tagged resources in the shared account cannot be assigned per business unit, and this changes pro forma billing rather than providing a Cost Explorer chargeback view.
o.C: Works but needs custom queries and maintenance, and does not feed AWS Budgets.
o.D: Ignores tagged resources in the shared account and provides no proportional allocation of shared costs.

d: LEAST operational overhead; in proportion to each business unit's own spend
